articles.title: Lift at Derker Tram Stop Out of Service Until Further Notice
articles.excerpt: The lift at Derker tram stop is currently out of service, affecting access for passengers. Step-free access is available via alternative routes until further notice.
articles.content_html:
The lift at Derker tram stop has been out of service since 8:09pm on 18 August 2026, impacting passengers using the tram service. There is currently no confirmed date for when the lift will be restored.

For customers travelling towards Manchester, step-free access is available via a ramp from Cromford Street directly to the Manchester-bound platform. Passengers heading towards Rochdale can also use a ramp from Cromford Street, followed by a track crossing to access the Rochdale-bound platform.

Transport for Greater Manchester has apologised for any inconvenience caused by this disruption and is advising passengers to plan their journeys accordingly. Passengers are encouraged to check the latest travel alerts on the Transport for Greater Manchester website for ongoing updates regarding the lift's status and any other travel disruptions.

Further information can be found on the Transport for Greater Manchester website, where live travel alerts are regularly updated.

articles.title: Rochdale Council Launches Good Food Strategy to Enhance Local Food Access
articles.excerpt: The Good Food Strategy aims to improve access to healthy and sustainable food across Rochdale, involving residents and businesses in its implementation.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Borough Council has launched its Good Food Strategy, which aims to ensure that healthy, affordable, and sustainable food is accessible to all residents. The strategy outlines collaboration with community groups, businesses, and partners to enhance food availability in the borough.

Key actions include increasing access to nutritious food, building food skills and confidence among residents, and strengthening local food networks. The initiative also seeks to celebrate Rochdale's diverse food culture.

This strategy reflects the council's commitment to addressing food insecurity and promoting healthier eating habits. Residents and local businesses are encouraged to participate in the strategy's implementation.

Further details can be found on the Rochdale Borough Council website.

articles.title: Plans for 450 New Homes on Former Green Belt Land in Bamford
articles.excerpt: Developers are moving forward with plans to build hundreds of homes on former green belt land in Bamford, following the removal of its protected status in 2024.
articles.content_html:
Hundreds of new homes are set to be built on former green belt land in Bamford, Rochdale, as developers ramp up plans for the area. A total of 450 houses have been earmarked for construction following the adoption of the Greater Manchester-wide Places for Everyone plan in 2024, which removed the land's protected status.

Northstone, a subsidiary of The Peel Group, is currently preparing a hybrid planning application for 350 homes on the western edge of the site off Norden Road. The proposed development will be divided into two phases, with 140 homes planned for the southern plot and 210 for the northern plot. The plans include high-quality, energy-efficient homes, new cycle and walking routes, two children's play areas, and a green linear park.

In addition to Northstone's plans, other developers have also submitted applications for the area, including Wain Homes, which proposes 45 homes, and McCarthy and Stone, which aims to build 67 retirement homes. However, Wain Homes' application faced delays earlier this month due to concerns over drainage issues raised by the council's planning committee, which requested further information before proceeding.

Councillor Tom Besford expressed concerns about the lack of an overarching masterplan for the 450 homes, fearing that the piecemeal approach could lead to inadequate benefits for the community, such as affordable housing. Northstone anticipates submitting its planning application to Rochdale Council by the end of 2026, and local residents are currently being consulted on the proposals.

articles.title: George Street Roadworks Scheduled for 1 October 2026 in Rochdale
articles.excerpt: Roadworks on George Street in Rochdale will result in a temporary closure on 1 October 2026, affecting traffic flow in the area.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Borough Council has announced that part of George Street will be temporarily closed on Thursday, 1 October 2026, due to scheduled roadworks. The closure will take place from midnight to 11.59pm, affecting the section of road 20 metres south of the junction with Ramsay Street to 20 metres north of the same junction.

During this period, no waiting will be permitted in the closed section of George Street. Local roads including Entwisle Road, Nile Street, Ramsay Street, Kitchen Street, and Norreys Street may experience increased traffic as drivers seek alternative routes.

Residents and motorists are advised to plan their journeys accordingly, as the roadworks could lead to delays. The council has provided a map of the roadworks across Greater Manchester for those wishing to navigate around the affected area.

Further updates regarding the roadworks and any potential changes to the schedule will be communicated by Rochdale Borough Council as the date approaches.

articles.title: Rochdale Valiant Launches New Media Portal for Local Community
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Valiant has introduced a new media portal aimed at providing contemporary news and information for the community.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Valiant has launched a new media portal designed to serve as a contemporary news source for the local community. The initiative aims to provide timely and relevant information, enhancing public engagement and awareness.

The portal, described as 'Rochdale's Media Portal for a New Generation and the 21st Century', focuses on delivering news and media content that reflects the interests and needs of residents.

This new platform is part of a broader effort to improve public communication and ensure that local voices are heard. It promises to offer a range of features including news articles, community updates, and public service announcements.

Residents are encouraged to visit the portal at Rochdale Valiant for updates on local developments and to engage in community discussions.
